In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the concentrations of organochlorines in Cormorant egg samples from Alberta were generally lower than those reported for the Great Lakes, and would not adversely affect Cormorant reproduction or eggshell thinning.
there is no evidence of a deleterious effect of organochlorines on Cormorant eggs or young in Alberta.
the concentrations of organochlorines detected in the Cormorants were not high enough to cause reproductive or physiological impairment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DDT, DDE and PCB levels are not of major concern in Alberta.
DDE and PCB residues are not affecting Cormorant reproductive potential, and that the PCB: DDE ratio in Cormorant tissue is an index of the local food chain contamination with these compounds.
organochlorine residues in Cormorants are not a major concern in Alberta, but the potential for bioaccumulation of PCBs in Cormornants is evident.
The main takeaway from our work is that
juvenile Cormorants are not exposed to significant concentrations of organochlorines.
the Cormorant is a useful indicator of organochlorines in aquatic ecosystems, especially in the Great Lakes region.
juvenile Cormorants can be used as regional indicators of contamination and provide a temporal view of the changes in contamination in aquatic ecosystems.
